Context marker: INTERVIEW-103-06b40c570a567729.

The bug is in `src/core.mjs`: `q.length>capacity` rejects pushes only after the queue already exceeds capacity. The contract requires rejection when `q.length >= capacity`.

Smallest valid counterexample: `solve(0, [["push", 1]])`. Initially, `q.length` is 0, so `0 > 0` is false; the code admits the item and returns `[true]`, leaving one item despite zero capacity. Required behavior is `[false]`, with the queue remaining empty. No implementation changes made.

automatic.answer: This is a small, dependency-free JavaScript service that simulates a capacity-limited FIFO queue, returning admission results for pushes and values or null for pops. Its architecture has a synchronous core, `solve(capacity, operations)` in `src/core.mjs`, a thin `execute` wrapper in `src/service.mjs`, and a Node.js smoke test run with `npm test`. The core currently has an off-by-one bug: it rejects pushes only when the queue length is greater than capacity, rather than greater than or equal to capacity, allowing one extra item.

This is a small, dependency-free JavaScript queue-admission service that simulates a capacity-limited FIFO queue. Its synchronous core, `solve(capacity, operations)` in `src/core.mjs`, returns admission booleans for pushes and FIFO values or `null` for pops; the current `q.length >= capacity` check prevents overfilling. `src/service.mjs` provides a thin `execute` wrapper, and `npm test` runs a Node.js smoke test through that wrapper.
